items.title: Discover BOT VFX's hybrid AI VFX pipeline for Young Washington
items.excerpt: BOT VFX delivered 300 shots in 17 weeks for Young Washington, mixing generative AI (FLUX.2 Klein, Wan) with a Maya/Nuke pipeline: AI crowd extensions, muzzle flashes and near-fully generated town shots. Temporal inconsistency, 4K upscaling and bit-depth limits meant heavy cleanup.
items.rationale: A concrete production breakdown (300 shots, 17 weeks) showing exactly where gen-AI fit into a Maya/Nuke pipeline and where it needed cleanup. Assigned to movies only by the brief.

items.title: Screenweaver adds AI-powered production platform to script editor
items.excerpt: Screenweaver's beta production platform turns an ingested script into an editable storyboard (frame, angle, movement, duration), generates AI scenes from it using Seedance, and exports to DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro. It plans AI audio and human-vs-AI provenance tracking.
items.rationale: A new tool release that goes from script to editable storyboard to generated scenes and exports to Resolve/Premiere, a usable previs workflow.

items.title: Ahmad Alameldeen Talks 'Safe Zone,' AI, and Starving Victims of War
items.excerpt: The Oscar-qualified animated short 'Safe Zone' pairs hand-drawn graphite and Procreate frames with motion generated in Kling. The director says AI tools struggled most with human emotion, especially a child in distress.
items.rationale: A hybrid workflow from an Oscar-qualified short: hand-drawn and Procreate keyframes animated in Kling, with a specific account of where the AI failed (human emotion).

items.title: AI Films From Kerala to the Andaman Islands Set for WIF India x Google Flow Filmathon, Screen at IFFI Goa
items.excerpt: Five films made with Google Flow were picked from 850+ registrations for WIF India's first AI Filmathon and screen at IFFI Goa.
items.rationale: Results, not a call for entries: five Google Flow films picked from 850+ registrations screen at a major festival (IFFI Goa). Assigned to movies only by the brief.

items.title: Doc filmmakers talk using AI as European plans for creating 'transparent' AI tools revealed
items.excerpt: At IDFA, the first edition to require AI-use disclosure in applications, Brazilian documentary makers describe using AI to 'fabulate' their film's revolutionary climax from archive photos without an on-screen disclaimer. European plans for transparent AI tools were also presented.
items.rationale: A new European plan for transparent AI filmmaking tools, unveiled at IDFA, plus documentary makers describing how they actually used AI with archive photos. Relevant to anyone working under disclosure rules.

https://www.screendaily.com/features/doc.new_action: European plans to build 'transparent' AI tools for filmmakers were presented at IDFA. This is a new announcement; the 11-19 card covered only IDFA's AI-disclosure requirement.
